question: Using the Let's Encrypt post at https://letsencrypt.org/2024/12/05/ending-ocsp/, what is Let's Encrypt ending, what replaces it, what are the key dates, and what is the main reason?

facts.claim: Let's Encrypt is ending OCSP support and will provide certificate revocation information only via CRLs.
facts.evidence: source line 686: "ending support for providing certificate revocation information via the"

facts.claim: On May 7, 2025, OCSP URLs are removed from certificates (and requests with the OCSP Must-Staple extension fail).
facts.evidence: source line 693: "<li>May 7, 2025"; source line 696: "On this date we will drop OCSP URLs from certificates"

facts.claim: On August 6, 2025, the OCSP responders are turned off.
facts.evidence: source line 700: "<li>August 6, 2025"; source line 702: "On this date we will turn off our OCSP responders"

facts.claim: The main reason is privacy: OCSP lets the CA learn which sites a visitor's IP address is visiting.
facts.evidence: source line 709: "We plan to end support for OCSP primarily because it represents a considerable risk to privacy on the Internet."

question: Using the Rust blog post at https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/04/04/docsrs-only-default-targets/, what change is docs.rs making and from when, which target is built by default, and what should a crate that needs documentation for more targets do?

facts.claim: Starting 2026-05-01, docs.rs builds documentation only for the default target (instead of five targets) when a crate does not list its targets.
facts.evidence: source line 92: "docs.rs will make a breaking change to its build"; source line 96: "list of five targets."; source line 98: "the default target unless additional targets are requested explicitly."

facts.claim: Unless default-target is set, the default target is x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.
facts.evidence: source line 112: "servers: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu."

facts.claim: A crate that needs more targets must list them all explicitly with `targets` under [package.metadata.docs.rs] in Cargo.toml.
facts.evidence: source line 119: "define the full list explicitly in your Cargo.toml"
